newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened mildly against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies following several interventions by the Bank of Israel, dealers said.
"When the session opened the basket was trading at 7.08 percent below the slope. The central bank intervened in the market several times, buying foreign currency," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against the basket of key currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency. Dealers said the central bank intervened many times and on a higher scale than in the last few days.
"The central bank was the main player today," Sadeh said.

Figures published by the Bank of Israel show that since the beginning of 1996 the basket has lost 1.61 percent in annual terms. In August alone the basket lost 0.67 percent. The dollar has gained 0.33 percent in annual terms since the beginning of the year but fell 0.35 percent last month.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1440 against 3.1420 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5402 shekels against 3.5394 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8823 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8979 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1210 shekels per mark against 2.1230 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1460 shekels.
